newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSI hopes China will join in its iron plant.
newsitem.headline: AUSI hopes China will join in its iron plant.

text.p: The managing director of AUSI Ltd, Patrick Patterson, said on Wednesday he was hopeful that China would participate in the company's A$1.9 billion direct reduced iron (DRI) project in the state of Western Australia.
Patterson told Reuters "we have reason to believe we are well positioned to see .. (Chinese) involvement".

He was commenting on an earlier statement by Prime Minister John Howard that Chinese Premier Li Ping had agreed to an Australian proposal to examine Chinese participation in a new iron processing plant in Western Australia.
Howard, speaking during a radio interview with Australian Broadcasting Corp from Beijing, did not identify the plant.
Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd is also planning a A$1.5 billion iron plant in the state, based on the hot briquetted iron system. Both would provide feedstock for steelmaking.

One of AUSI Ltd's founders, Sir Russell Madigan, was a member of the high-powered business delegation accompanying the prime minister on his trip, which ended on Wednesday. Patterson pointed to Madigan's inclusion in the trip when asked if AUSI was the favoured contender for Chinese participation.
Another AUSI founder is former Australian Ambassador to China, Ross Garnaut.
The AUSI DRI project is a privately-owned venture in which one of the major participants is the Norwegian-based international engineering group Kvaerner ASA.
Patterson was appointed managing director of Australian United Steel Industry Ltd (AUSI) last December following Kvaerner's entry onto AUSI's share register.

Last month Patterson told a conference in Sydney that AUSI "expects to be in a position to proceed with a capital-raising programme involving both debt and equity financing in Australia and internationally through to financial close in the first quarter of 1998".
